claim_ledger.claim: The University of Copenhagen confirmed a data breach affecting 525,000 people.
Hackers accessed a test environment containing personal data of 525,000 people.
The breach was detected on October 20, 2026, and disclosed on October 23, 2026.
An additional 20,000 staff and students had their PIN codes exposed in an update on October 25, 2026.
The University of Copenhagen is still investigating the extent of the breach.
The breach may have exposed full names, national identity numbers, phone numbers, and email addresses.
The university restricted physical access to some critical locations on campus as a precaution.
The university says it contained the attack and blocked the attacker’s access.
The breach falls within the scope of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
The university reported the incident to the Danish Data Protection Agency.
Students and staff are advised to be cautious of unsolicited communications and verify requests independently.
The university promised to provide more updates on the impact as its internal investigation allows.
